gaps.sentence: By the end of the month, they ___ the new bridge.
gaps.hint: by the end of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a specific future point takes the future perfect: will have finished.

gaps.sentence: This perfume ___ of roses and vanilla.
gaps.hint: perceived smell is a state verb
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception like 'smell' are state verbs, so the present simple is used: smells.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ the presentation started when the fire alarm went off.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly had … when' — the past perfect with inversion after 'hardly'.

gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.

gaps.sentence: Every morning she ___ an hour in the garden before breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' marks a repeated routine, which takes the present simple: spends.

gaps.sentence: She has bought the paint, so tomorrow she ___ the kitchen.
gaps.hint: an intention already decided before speaking
gaps.explanation: An intention decided before the moment of speaking uses 'be going to': is going to paint.
